parsed.title: Discussion on AI in Job Search and Development

topics.title: AI tools for job searching and resume generation

claims.text: The author plans to set up a cloud (OpenClaw) to automate job search, PDF resume generation for specific vacancies, and cover letter writing.
AI-generated resumes can be analyzed by humans during technical interviews, unlike plain white text.
Lack of AI skills (e.g., Cursor, Claude Code, LLM, RAG, Embeddings) makes job hunting for JS/Python positions very difficult in 2026.
The acceleration of development claims started becoming real only in 2025, with tools becoming both better and more expensive.
The author expects the recruiting profession to become obsolete, envisioning HR as purely personnel management.

topics.title: AI-assisted code generation and its pitfalls

claims.text: Using LLMs (e.g., GPT) to generate join queries and other code significantly accelerates development by handling routine tasks.
Generated code can be unsafe, producing overly large raw SQL queries that risk security and performance (e.g., a 450-line query pulling all user data).
Incremental computation ideas were replaced by views, indicating a shift in optimization strategies.
Some engineers push unreviewed, low‑quality code (e.g., SELECT *) to production, sometimes after AI‑generated code that breaks the project.
Automatic database schema recreation on changes caused additional confusion in a company.

topics.title: Future of recruiters and candidate sourcing

claims.text: Candidate search using keyword filters is becoming detached from reality.
The author anticipates the recruiter profession will die out, with HR handling only personnel management.

topics.title: Using logs for debugging and knowledge limits of models

claims.text: The author suggests logging (e.g., in JUnit) could help AI identify recurring issues earlier.
Simple models cannot capture the accumulated context and nuanced decisions present in a developer's mind.
Long debugging sessions may become futile if logs are not helpful for understanding requirements.
If one struggles too long, the outcome may be suboptimal.
